name: Diblaim
title: Gomer's father
summary: Diblaim is known from the Bible solely as the father of Gomer, the woman whom the prophet Hosea was commanded by God to marry. He is mentioned only once in Scripture, in Hosea 1:3, and his significance lies in his connection to the prophet Hosea's symbolic marriage.

keyEvents.title: Diblaim is mentioned as Gomer's father
keyEvents.description: Diblaim is mentioned in connection with the prophet Hosea taking Gomer, Diblaim's daughter, as his wife by God's command. This marriage was to serve as a prophetic sign of God's relationship with unfaithful Israel.

keyEvents.title: God's command regarding the marriage
keyEvents.description: God commanded Hosea to take an unfaithful wife as a symbolic sign of Israel's unfaithfulness toward God. Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, was chosen for this purpose.

keyEvents.title: Gomer's first child, Jezreel
keyEvents.description: After the marriage between Hosea and Gomer, Diblaim's daughter, their first son Jezreel was born, named as a prophetic sign against the house of Jehu.

keyEvents.title: Hosea's Prophetic Message Through His Family
keyEvents.description: Through his marriage to Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, and their children, Hosea conveyed a powerful message about God's love and judgment over Israel.
